root_cause.text: The `vti6_tnl_lookup()` function in `net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c` fails to verify that a candidate tunnel's endpoint is a wildcard address during fallback searches, leading to incorrect tunnel matches when hash collisions occur in the shared `tnls_r_l` hash table.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)` and `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)` checks to the fallback search loops in `vti6_tnl_lookup()` to ensure the candidate tunnel actually has a wildcard address.

intent_record.how: Ensures that the lookup for wildcard-remote tunnels only matches tunnels configured with an unspecified remote address, preventing incorrect matches on tunnels with specific remote addresses.

intent_record.what: Added a check to verify if the tunnel's local IPv6 address is unspecified (any) during the lookup loop.
intent_record.how: This restricts the lookup match to only return tunnels with an unspecified local address when performing a wildcard search, preventing incorrect tunnel matching.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.

Currently we can't lookup tunnels with wildcard endpoint
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit fbe68ee87522f6eaa10f9076c0a7117e1613f2f7
Author: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 20 10:01:49 2014 +0100

    vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.
    
    Currently we can't lookup tunnels with wildcard endpoints.
    This patch adds a method to lookup these tunnels in the
    receive path.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
index d440bb58552
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the fallback searches in `vti6_tnl_lookup()` but fails to verify that the matched tunnel actually has a wildcard endpoint. Specifically, in the first fallback loop (lines 107-112), it only checks `ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr)` without verifying `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)`. In the second fallback loop (lines 114-119), it only checks `ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr)` without verifying `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)`. If a hash collision occurs in the `tnls_r_l` hash table, a tunnel with fully-specified endpoints can be incorrectly matched.
